recipes.name: Easy Butternut Squash Ravioli
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, or to taste

steps.text: Place mashed squash into a mixing bowl. Add salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir in mascarpone cheese, egg yolk, and 1/3 cup Parmesan cheese, mixing until filling is combined.

Place a wonton wrapper onto a working surface. Wet the tip of a finger in water, and run it all along the outer edge of the wonton skin to moisten. Place about 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of the wonton.
Fold the wonton in half to make a half-moon shape, and press the edges to seal. Repeat with the remaining wonton wrappers.
Place a deep skillet over medium-low heat. Stir in butter and unpeeled clove of garlic.
Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a boil. Drop filled ravioli into boiling water, a few at a time, and cook until they float to the top, about 2 minutes.
Drain ravioli, and transfer to the skillet. Increase heat to medium-high, and cook just until ravioli are infused with garlic butter flavor, about 2 or 3 more minutes.
Serve hot; sprinkle with chopped sage, more black pepper, and extra Parmesan cheese to taste.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Butternut Squash Ravioli
raw_recipe.description: Butternut squash ravioli filled with roasted butternut squash, mascarpone, and sage. This easy recipe from Chef John uses wonton wrappers instead of pasta.

review.reviewBody: These were super delicious! This will definitely be a regular item on my family's dinner menu. My only gripe about this recipe is the delicacy of the won ton wrapper. It took several tries to prevent tearing and to sufficently seal the edges together. Once mastered though, this recipe rocked! I followed another reviewer's advice and used a generous amount of cayenne pepper which gave the ravioli a nice kick. In case anyone else doesn't have mascarpone cheese stocked in their fridge, a mixture of 8 oz. cream cheese, 2 1/2 tbs sour cream, and 1/4 c. heavy whipping cream in lieu of the mascarpone cheese works perfectly.

My entire family (kids included!) love these ravioli! They are time consuming, but well worth the effort. Fresh sage and roasted garlic in the browned (plant-based) butter make this spectacular, as does a sprinkle of fresh parmesan cheese on top and the cayenne pepper in the filling. I increase the cheese a bit, and then I puree my filling in my Ninja. For me, one batch of the filling makes two packs of wonton ravioli, so I usually make a double batch of the filling and use one portion while freezing three in vacuum bags. Then, when I want to make them, I just defrost the filling and cut the end of the bag so I can pipe it right into the wonton wrapper. I've also frozen the cooked ravioli, vacuum sealed with parchment in between layers, with success. Just pop them into a little brown butter to reheat, add a side salad and you've got a super quick dinner.

This was really good as it, but also makes a great finger food with minor modifications. I used a small paint brush to brush the water on the edges before sealing. Keeps things less messy.
Here are some mods:
1. if you want less sweet, substitute ricotta cheese for the marscapone.
2. If you want to serve as finger food appetizer, put the raviolis on a cookie sheet (cover with foil, light mist of olive oil) and mist with olive oil. PAM sells olive oil spray or you can use a mister bottle to get a light olive oil spray. Cook at 350 for about 10 minutes and the raviolis will have a nice crunch.
3. If you want raviolis baked but not crunchy (to serve on plate with sauce), leave out the spray of olive oil and just cook on cookie sheet with foil and non-stick spray.

Play around with these, they are really delicious.

Really liked this filling. Rather than use the won ton wrappers, used semolina flour and rolled out the dough in our pasta machine. Used the filling from this recipe. They came out great. Sauted the boiled ravioli in butter and a couple cloves of minced garlic.

I have made these often, sometimes using ricotta cheese mixed with the squash. I cook them like pot stickers, a little water in a large frying pan, covered, then let water cook off so they get browned on the bottom. Delicious with a butter sage sauce and toasted pumpkin seeds!

These were really simple and delicious! I used leftover roasted squash and subbed cottage cheese for the mascarpone ( to cut fat, budget and richness of the meal) and my store only had the square wonton wrappers. * I did add more cayenne for an extra a kick. I prepared the filling late in the afternoon, then covered it and let it chill in the fridge. When dinner time approached, I heated the oven for the salmon and asparagus (with their seasonings) and started boiling the water for the dumplings. Threw the things in the oven and started filling the pasta. After the dumplings are in the water, when they return to boil, turn the heat on the butter in the skillet....yadda, yadda... less than thirty minutes work and it was a beautiful meal! Will do these again!

Delicate flavor, not over-powering, just creamy yumminess. I didn't have mascarpone cheese, so I used cream cheese with whipping cream as a substitute. Also, these make enough for at least 4 people, and they take a long time to fill/pinch/boil; therefore, I suggest doing what I did--put some olive oil on a couple big plates and after boiling slide them around in the oil, then let them cool. Do not stack (which I did and they stuck together on my first 7), and boil in small batches. After they cooled, I put them on a layer of wax paper over the more cool ones. I let them set until dinner time at which time I warmed them up in the pan with the garlic oil.

I liked this a lot. I made a double batch of the filling and ended up using all 45 of my round wonton wrappers and still had some leftover! Luckily this doesn't bother me because I enjoyed the finished product. (I froze the rest, uncooked, flat on parchment paper, then moved them into a Ziploc baggie with a bit of cornstarch to help prevent sticking.)

I made two changes to the recipe, one out of necessity--cream cheese over mascarpone because mine went bad--and one because I preferred it after tasting, and that was to add nutmeg and a pack of Equal to the butter sauce. Next time, I would probably add a bit of heavy cream to it, too. Definitely a recommended recipe!

Tasted amazing. The store was all out of butternut squash, so I used baked acorn squash with a bit of brown sugar and blended to a creamy consistency in a blender. It tasted just as good. The wonton wrappers were easy to use (make sure to keep your hands and workplace dry when working with them, or else they become sticky) but the ravioli stuck together after cooking, so maybe they should be brushed with olive oil right after cooking next time. I also did not fry the ravioli in butter and garlic and the taste was still great. I made this for 25 people and it was highly enjoyed.

I thought it was great! I added some dried marjoram to the spices inside. I made them and froze them. Doubled recipe, made 53 dumplings with leftover filling. I stuffed small zucchini and baked with some Mozzarella on top. Even my husband loved it and he doesn’t like zucchini!

Like others, I made a lot of changes to adjust for what I had on hand. The result was fabulous (as I imagine the original recipe is)! I used acorn squash and used goat cheese instead of mascarpone. I increased the squash:cheese ratio a bit since the goat cheese has such a strong tang and could easily overpower the mix. It was delicious! I recommend adding the egg last so you can taste and adjust as needed beforehand. I also made a cream sauce, starting with the butter and smashed garlic, adding a little wine, and then adding half and half. I have also found the secret to any good italian cream sauce is a couple of dashes of nutmeg. You won't be disappointed! Finally, adding a little oil to the boiling water will help prevent the raviolis from sticking together and to the pan. This is certainly a keeper!
I love to make pasta so I stuck with traditional ravioli and followed the recipe without changing a thing. Definitely one of our new favorite meals!

YUM!!! This was incredible. The filling was extremely flavorful and it came together in a snap. I made as written but didn't have any sage but I think that would make this even better. I went for two wrappers per ravioli for a more traditional look. This would make the perfect meatless Monday dinner. Thanks, Chef John!
Filling is amazing, struggled with the wonton wraps
This is so rich and delish! instead of marscapone i used a mix of cream cheese and cottage cheese. so good!!

Another Chef John winner! Everyone loved it! Used my first harvested butternut squash and homegrown sage. Better than any restaurant. Thought the unpeeled garlic was weird but the garlic flavor was perfect.
Fabulous!!!

Thank you so much for sharing this great recipe. A little time consuming but my vegetarian kids LOVED it!!! The next time I think I will try cottage cheese instead of cream cheese, a little more squash:cheese in the ratio, and dried sage inside the ravioli.

I didn't boil them. I cooked them like I do potstickers. Sauteed with a bit of butter spray, then small amount of water to steam them for 40 secs or so. Delish! Also didn't use marscapone cheese. Used cream cheese.

This is fab. I didn't change the ingredients, just the technique to make this easier. 
I had a 2 lb + a few ozs. squash yielding two full cups of cooked squash. Peeling and cutting butternut squash is a chore. So, I cut the squash in half and removed seeds then roasted cut side down at 400 degrees for about 45-60 minutes. I feel the squash benefits from a little caramelization when roasted. When cool, I simply scooped the squash from the shells. I did this early in the day giving the squash plenty of time to cool. 
I used 3 " square wonton wrappers and made large ravioli by putting two wraps together which I thought would be quicker than smaller ones. I used the egg white with a tablespoon or so water to seal them. Had no problems with leakage. Six of these large ravioli was a generous meal. I did mince the garlic so that it was incorporated into the butter sauce and into our mouths! and added about a tablespoon fresh minced sage to the garlic butter after I had turned off the heat. I let this sit before cooking the raviolis.
I only cooked 4 at a time. I put the raviolis into a a shallow dish as I cooked each batch and poured a of the little butter sauce over each layer. Pouring the butter sauce over the ravioli rather than putting them in the pan I think made retrieving them easier, as the "wonton"ravioli, though convenient and tasty, are a bit more fragile than pasta dough.
